title: Molecular Transformer: Template-Free Deep Learning for Organic Reaction Prediction
whyItMatters: First template-free Transformer to surpass 90% top-1 accuracy on organic reaction outcome prediction directly from SMILES strings, beating human organic chemists while quantifying its own uncertainty.
summary: Philippe Schwaller, Teodoro Laino, Théophile Gaudin, Jean-Louis Reymond, and colleagues (IBM Research Zurich & University of Bern) published the Molecular Transformer in ACS Central Science (2019), formulating organic reaction prediction as machine translation between reactant and product SMILES strings. Eliminating hand-coded reaction templates and atom-mapping heuristics entirely, the multi-head attention model surpassed 90% top-1 accuracy on the USPTO-MIT benchmark—outperforming both graph-based models and expert human chemists—while accurately predicting subtle regio-, chemo-, and stereoselectivity and powering the widely used IBM RXN for Chemistry cloud platform.
technicalHighlights: Achieved >90% top-1 accuracy on the standard USPTO-MIT organic reaction benchmark without hand-crafted reaction templates or explicit atom mapping.
Provided calibrated prediction uncertainty (0.89 ROC-AUC for separating correct from erroneous predictions) and outperformed human chemists in head-to-head tests.
Generalized to complex multi-step natural-product and pharmaceutical reactions including stereoselective and carbohydrate transformations.
caveats: Relies on patent-derived training corpora (USPTO) that under-represent negative/failed reactions, organometallic mechanisms, and exact experimental yields.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated that template-free Transformer attention learns chemical reactivity, selectivity, and stoichiometry directly from text representations.
scoreRationale.ripple: Became the canonical paradigm for neural reaction prediction, retrosynthesis, and automated IBM RXN RoboRXN synthesis.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in ACS Central Science with open-source code, public benchmarks, and global adoption across chemistry labs.
scoreRationale.velocity: Enabled millisecond in-silico screening of thousands of candidate organic reactions prior to wet-lab trials.

sources.label: ACS Central Science (2019): Molecular Transformer: A Model for Uncertainty-Calibrated Chemical Reaction Prediction
